architecture.mechanism: Colloidal monolayer membranes (CMMs) formed by anisotropic particles increase bending rigidity, enabling uniform deposition of particles during evaporation and reducing edge accumulation.
architecture.intervention: Embed ellipsoidal or anisotropic nanoparticles (e.g., graphene flakes, nanorods) into the leading-edge composite blade surface to form a CMM-like protective layer. Apply a surfactant-compatible coating to maintain Marangoni flow dynamics during rain/hail impact, promoting uniform erosion resistance.
architecture.expected_effect: Reduced localized erosion at the leading edge by distributing impact forces uniformly across the blade surface, minimizing energy production loss and delaying repair campaigns.
architecture.falsification_test: Compare erosion rates of blade sections coated with ellipsoidal nanoparticles vs. spherical nanoparticles (control) after controlled rain/hail exposure in a wind tunnel. Measure surface roughness and material loss via 3D scanning; validate uniform deposition via cross-sectional microscopy.
